title: Sephiria Companion Build — Summoner Route (Pets, Ballista, Tablets)
description: Sephiria companion build: the summoner route — Companion-tagged Artifacts, Ballista, and Tablets on summons, plus Dimensional Pocket carry.
meta: For sephiria companion build / summoner searches.
body:
sephiria companion build is a summoner route: stack Companion-tagged Artifacts, run Ballista beside them, and put Tablets on summons so pets soak aggro while you finish elites and bosses. This page covers the route's pieces and the order to assemble them; the builds overview covers every theme, and the Artifacts and Tablets page explains the grid rules the route depends on.

Core idea

  • Prioritize Companion family items early (contracts, moles, jellyfish, cushions, etc.). Community clear videos treat “get all companions online” as the first-floor job.
  • Ballista / mine-crossbow evolutions play like extra companions once mines become seeking drones.
  • Put Tablets and buffs on companions, not on random side DPS tags.
  • Companions are expensive to max—Dimensional Pocket / Willpower lines that carry items between runs make the build much smoother.

How the build works, as far as it is documented

Three systems do the work, and each one is described in more detail elsewhere on the site. The first is the Companion combo tag: the family is a set of Artifacts that spawn or buff a summon — contracts, moles, jellyfish, cushions and similar pieces — and those pieces only pay out when several of them are active together. The second is the mine-crossbow line, where Ballista-style upgrades keep firing while you reposition; once mines become seeking drones, the effect reads like one more pet on the field. The third is Tablets, which buff patterns covering several inventory slots rather than a single item, so their value depends on where the Companion pieces sit.

None of that is a hidden interaction. The route works for a mundane reason: summons keep drawing enemy attention, and that buys the time a low personal-DPS board needs to finish elites and bosses. A player report on the Steam forums describes the pairing from the other side — blocking through the final boss phases with Sword and Shield while companions dealt the damage, with mana regeneration paying for the block. That is one player's clear, not a guarantee for your run, but it matches the logic of the build.

What to take and why

PieceWhat it does hereWhen to take it
Companion-family Artifacts (contracts, moles, jellyfish, cushions)The build itself. Each piece adds a summon or strengthens summons already on the field.Floor one, before any damage tag
Ballista / mine-crossbow upgradesA second damage source that keeps working while you dodge, and later mine behaviour reads like extra companions.As your second tag, once the Companion family is stable
TabletsBuff the pattern (line, cross, column) covering your Companion pieces. An Artifact outside an active pattern wastes a slot.Whenever one pattern covers two or more Companion items
Wishing Fountain picksPre-run Artifact selection in town. The slots are most useful spent on Companion pieces you already know you want.After the unlock, and only once the weapon family is chosen
Tactical Manual (Companion + Precision bond)Routes companion damage through crit. It only switches on when both tags are already present.After Precision is genuinely part of the build, never before
Dimensional Pocket / Willpower progressCarry lines that reduce how much of the set you rebuild every run.Between runs, as a long-term spend
Fruit SkewersBias which combo families the run offers you.When Companion offers keep drying up
Side BagStorage only. Items inside contribute no effects, Tablets included.For pieces you intend to swap in later

Sources: the Artifacts and Tablets page (Tablet geometry, bond tag pairings, Side Bag), the Wishing Fountain page (pre-run picks and unlock route), the beginner guide (Fruit Skewers, Side Bag), and the Steam Companion discussion listed in Sources. The bond pairing comes from a player-maintained index, not from the developer, so verify the current effect text in your Journal.

The order to assemble it

Most failed versions of this build pick Artifacts before deciding what the Artifacts are for. Assemble in this order instead.

  1. Weapon family first. Choose the branch you will actually play and read its upgrade pool before floor one. The companion route usually leans on the mine-crossbow line because Ballista-style upgrades keep working without your input. The weapons page lists the six branches and how their evolution routes chain.
  2. Companion tag second. Take Companion Artifacts over anything shinier until the family is stacked. One mole or jellyfish is a distraction; four of them start acting like a build.
  3. Wishing Fountain picks third. If the fountain is unlocked through Destiny New Events, fill the slots with Companion pieces. Community notes put default capacity at 4 with higher rarity costing more of the bar, and Willpower raising the ceiling — treat those figures as reported rather than current, and confirm in-game. Players also report that bond Artifacts are not offered there, so do not build the plan around buying Tactical Manual from the fountain.
  4. Ballista or another mine line fourth. Once the pets exist, add the second damage source. This is the point where the run stops depending entirely on summon uptime.
  5. Tablets before the first boss, not after. Tablets amplify the shape of the board, so place them while you can still rearrange slots. The Artifacts page covers adjacency and why geometry beats raw rarity.
  6. Carry lines between runs. Dimensional Pocket and Willpower progress is slow, but it is the difference between assembling the set in three floors and assembling it every run from zero.

Pairings other players report

The Steam thread behind this page pairs companions with Sword and Shield, and the reason given is practical: the shield branch has an interaction with Lightning Ballista summons, and blocking plus mana regeneration let that player stay in the fight while the companions dealt damage. The cost is mana. Guarding drains it, so the pairing only holds if the run can sustain regeneration; without that, the block drops and the pets inherit the fight alone.

A second reply in the same thread says the final boss ignores companions and always targets the player. If that is still true in your build, the aggro line buys you the floors before the last fight but not the last fight itself — plan a personal damage or defence answer for it rather than assuming the pets will tank. Test it in your own run before relying on either version.

Run habits

  • Accept Storm Cloud or light fire as secondary only if it supports Ballista/mines—do not dilute five tags.
  • In co-op, companions keep drawing aggro so human players can focus mechanics. Agree who spends Tablets before floor one, because the loot is shared. See the co-op guide.
  • After bosses, rebuild adjacency so Companion pieces stay bonded and Tablets still cover them.
  • Read the live description after every Anvil or Tablet choice. Upgrade text changes between patches, and a route name is not a guarantee that the effect still reads the same way.

Common mistakes

  • Spreading early picks across five families — companions only come online when the family is stacked.
  • Buffing your own damage while pets die — Tablets and level-ups belong on the summons.
  • Ignoring carry lines: without Dimensional Pocket / Willpower progress you rebuild the set every run.
  • Buying a bond Artifact before its second tag exists. A bond with a missing tag is a dead slot, not a discount.
  • Counting Side Bag pieces as active. Stored items contribute nothing, Tablets included, so the board you fight with is smaller than the inventory you own.

What this page cannot confirm

  • Item names and numbers. Community writeups use names that move between patches; per-level values and upgrade labels are not reproduced here for that reason. Check the Journal in your client.
  • Whether Ballista counts as a Companion. The tag list is the authority, and this page has not verified how mine and Ballista upgrades are tagged in the current build.
  • Fountain behaviour for bond Artifacts. The "not offered at the fountain" report comes from Steam discussion, not from patch notes.
  • Boss targeting. The claim that the final boss ignores summons is a single player report and may have changed.
  • Version. The public branch was 1.0.33 when the builds page was last checked, with the 1.1 workshop beta tracked separately. Anything from the beta belongs on the beta branch.

Questions people ask

What counts as a Companion item?

Contracts, moles, jellyfish, cushions and similar pet-family Artifacts — anything that spawns or buffs a summon. The reliable test is the combo tag shown on the item, not the name.

Do companions hold aggro?

Community clears use them as the aggro line while the player finishes elites and bosses, and in co-op they do the same job for the whole team. One player report says the final boss ignores them, so treat boss aggro as something to check rather than a rule.

Is it good for Hard Mode?

It is one of the themes players carry into Root’s Retreat stages; check the Hard Mode page for what changes. Because the build leans on uptime rather than burst, it rewards runs where you can keep the summons alive through the stage modifiers.

Should I pair it with Sword and Shield?

Only if the run can pay for guarding. The Steam report that pairs them relied on mana regeneration to hold block through the final boss; without that, the shield half of the plan collapses and you are back to pets alone.

How many Companion pieces do I need before it works?

There is no confirmed threshold in the sources used here. Community videos treat "get all companions online" as the first-floor job, which is the closest thing to a number: stack the family first, then judge whether the run has enough.

Theme-level consensus also appears in 9Puz / SlashSkill “commit to one combo family” advice. Exact item IDs shift with patches—use the Journal and this page’s video sources for current names.
